A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Cooperation of Experts (CoE) study. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification results in Tables 1–3, structural-perturbation experiments, and hyperparameter sensitivity analyses, including Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original classification, ablation, robustness, and sensitivity results in the main text and Appendix F.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E retain the same graph construction, two-level experts, mutual-information objectives, confidence tensor, and large-margin mechanism. Equation 1 moves between pages without changing the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ACM, DBLP, Yelp, MAG, and Amazon network classification and ESP, Flickr, IAPR, and NUS multimodal classification. The structural-perturbation scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 and Figure 3 retain identical comparator memberships: 15 network baselines, nine multimodal baselines, four ablation variants, and the same robustness comparators. The newly cited works are not added to the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 and Appendices B–C retain the accuracy metric, GCN backbone, best-individual-network baseline reporting rule, preprocessing, training settings, and data splits. Tables 5–7 contain the same settings and sample counts.

E4.justification: The RF, WRF, w/o HE, and w/o GSL ablations, ACM edge-addition/deletion tests, and sensitivity analyses for gamma, alpha, and K are unchanged. Appendix F contains the same analysis as before.

E5.justification: Appendix B states five runs with averaged results in both versions. Tables 1–3 retain the same accuracy-plus-standard-deviation reporting, with no added uncertainty estimation or significance testing.

E6.justification: The numerical entries and findings in Tables 1–3 and Figures 1 and 3–5 match. For example, CoE remains at 94.21 ± 0.14 on ACM and 81.11 ± 0.05 on ESP; the appendix sensitivity results also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorems 4.1 and 5.1–5.3, generalization derivation, and Appendix D proofs are unchanged. Citation updates and equation relocation introduce no new assumptions, reasoning, or formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about expert cooperation, large-margin optimization, theoretical guarantees, and performance across heterogeneous data. The novelty claims are neither expanded nor narrowed.

C2.justification: Both versions give the same interpretations of complementary expert knowledge, confidence weighting, GSL robustness, and the generalization tradeoff involving expert count. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: The code-access link and implementation disclosures remain unchanged. Appendices B, C, and E retain the hardware, PyTorch/DGL versions, Adam settings, hyperparameters, batch size, feature processing, and graph post-processing instructions.

R1.justification: Three unresolved citation locations in the introduction and Sections 2.1–2.2 are filled with five added works: Shen and Kang (2025), Qian et al. (2024), Xie et al. (2025), Li et al.'s PC-Conv, and Pan and Kang (2023). The surrounding research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The prose and section organization are essentially unchanged. Limited editorial changes repair citation callouts and replace several preprint records with conference publication details, although some updated author-year citations now omit their years.

P2.justification: All five figures and seven tables retain their content and design. Local reflow moves Equation 1 from page 3 to page 4 and slightly shifts Figure 4; the expanded bibliography leaves its final entry alone on page 12 and moves the appendices one page later.

improvement.justification: Replacing unresolved citations with identifiable references modestly improves attribution and traceability. The scientific content, evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged. Missing years in several updated citations and less compact pagination limit the editorial benefit, but the resolved references provide a small net improvement.
